source: can you make a game where your a cat and you have to scratch furniture to get money and with the money you can buy different cat patterns that makes you stronger and the map is a massive house and you are very small and it makes your avatar look like a cat

image_prompt.text: A central spot in the house where the cat spends money on new patterns and upgrades, the place the loop keeps returning to
Physical barriers closing off the pricier rooms of the house until the cat has earned enough to open them
Hallways and floor-level routes chaining the shop spot out to every room worth scratching in
Sofas, armchairs and table legs positioned as scratchable furniture, the repeatable earning station of the loop
Rooms and furniture drawn oversized so the player reads as a very small cat inside a massive house

layout_placement.text: Scratch stations on each piece of furniture that pay out money on a repeatable timer

notes: Mixed classification: the earning-and-upgrade loop is Simulation and owns the shape, while Roleplay and Avatar Sim covers the cat avatar. The roleplay file contributed no options - all of its shapes are settlements or open wilderness and this map is the inside of one house.
No genre shape can say the entire playable world is an interior; only the no-genre axis set has interior-only. world-shared was used and the interior nature is carried here instead.
The player is a very small cat, so the usual 16 studs per second walking assumption behind the scale band does not hold - the house should be framed for a much slower, smaller mover.

open_questions.ask: What kind of house - a cosy modern family home, something grand and old, or stylized and cartoon?
How small is the cat relative to the furniture? That decides whether a normal house needs to be built at two or three times normal size.
Is there an end to the loop - all patterns unlocked, all furniture destroyed - or does it just keep going?

coverage_missing.ask: How small is the cat relative to the furniture?
Does the loop end, or continue indefinitely?

answers.ask: What kind of house - a cosy modern family home, something grand and old, or stylized and cartoon?
answers.answer: Use a cosy modern family home, built with a playful cartoon style.

answers.ask: How small is the cat relative to the furniture? That decides whether a normal house needs to be built at two or three times normal size.
answers.answer: Make the cat very small relative to the furniture, with the house built at roughly three times normal scale so furniture feels huge.

answers.ask: Is there an end to the loop - all patterns unlocked, all furniture destroyed - or does it just keep going?
answers.answer: The game keeps going as an ongoing scratch-and-upgrade loop; the prompt does not call for a final ending.
